## Design

### 2026-11-03: First, i spent 1 hour planning the project, deciding specifics, and finding parts. the calculator runs on a raspberry pi pico, has a bunch of buttons (45 buttons may be a little too much, ill probably

**1.97h**

First, i spent 1 hour planning the project, deciding specifics, and finding parts. the calculator runs on a raspberry pi pico, has a bunch of buttons (45 buttons may be a little too much, ill probably cut it down later), a 2.42in oled screen(which is waay too expensive), a 3.7v lipo battery and a tp4056 battery charging and protection module.
next, i spent another hour designing the schematic (surprised i finished so quick). this i logged via lapse.

### 2026-11-05: made some small changed to the schematic(power flags, no connection flages, changed some connections, removed the battery connecter as ill just connect it directly to the tp4056), assigned footprints

**2.47h**

made some small changed to the schematic(power flags, no connection flages, changed some connections, removed the battery connecter as ill just connect it directly to the tp4056), assigned footprints (took way too long to decide the pushbuttons, but i think i got a good size) and started designing the pcb. placing and arranging the components took some time and i just started with the routing. i had to make sure the size of the pcb was within 100mmx100mm (first week i had a bigger pcb, and the price shot up). also using only 40 buttons, not 45.
